agent_summary:
Target juice.lab.test is OWASP Juice Shop (Angular SPA + Express/Node, SQLite + MongoDB) served over HTTP only (443 refused). I mapped the real surface from main.js (REST/API routes) and tested all 19 input-validation items with read-only requests (~120 exchanges).

KEY FINDINGS (leads recorded):
- CRITICAL SQL injection in GET /rest/products/search?q= — a quote yields a 500 SQLite error leaking the query; a UNION payload (q=qwert'))UNION SELECT sqlite_version(),'2'..'9'--) returned id="3.44.2" plus marker columns, proving arbitrary query execution (non-sensitive proof used; credentials not dumped).
- HIGH poison-null-byte extension bypass in /ftp: direct /ftp/*.bak is 403 ("only .md/.pdf"), but /ftp/<file>%2500.md returns 200 with the full restricted file (confirmed on package.json.bak, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg). nginx blocks encoded ../ traversal (400).
- HIGH data exposure: unauthenticated /rest/memories returns user objects incl. password hashes/email/tokens (admin + deluxe users) — flagged for authz/data lane.
- MEDIUM open redirect: /redirect allowlists targets by substring; /redirect?to=https://evil.example.com/?x=<allowlisted-url> 302s to the attacker domain. CRLF in the target is URL-encoded (no response splitting).
- LOW: verbose Express stack traces (file paths, version), internal localhost URL in security.txt, wildcard CORS (Origin not reflected).

TESTED / NOT VULNERABLE (done): reflected XSS (1 — server returns JSON / error pages HTML-escape; the search sink is client-side DOM only, noted); verb tampering (3 — OPTIONS enumerated GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE); HPP (4); SSI (8), format string (13), SSTI (18) — payloads to the reflecting /rest/track-order echo and search were stripped/returned literally, never evaluated ({{7*7}}→77); code injection (11) and command injection (12) — no execution on reachable params; HTTP splitting (15); HTTP methods (16); host header (17 — real Host pinned by gateway, X-Forwarded-Host not reflected). Finale CRUD routes (/api/*) are parameterized and mostly auth-gated (401/403); public endpoints: Products, Feedbacks(list), Quantitys(list), Deliverys, Recycles, SecurityQuestions, product reviews, languages, metrics, encryptionkeys listing, config/version.

NOT TESTED (N/A — require writes, which this read-only engagement forbids): stored XSS (2 — feedback comment field stores raw HTML, documented as sink), XML/XXE (7 — /file-upload POST), incubated (14), SSRF (19 — authenticated profile-image-URL fetch; the only read-only URL-fetch surface, /redirect, is a client-side open redirect not SSRF). LDAP (6), XPath (9), IMAP/SMTP (10) marked N/A: no such backend/interface exists (SQL + MongoDB only). TRACE could not be sent with the available tooling. /profile Pug-SSTI sink is guarded ("Blocked illegal activity") without a valid session.

leads.title: [agent] Open redirect via allowlist substring bypass in /redirect

detail.text: GET /redirect?to=https://evil.example.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop returned HTTP 302 with Location: https://evil.example.com/?x=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop. The endpoint allowlists known target URLs but only checks for their presence as a substring, so appending an allowlisted URL as a query parameter lets an attacker redirect victims to an arbitrary external domain. A plain arbitrary target (to=http://evil.example.com/) is rejected with 406.

leads.title: [agent] Poison null-byte extension-validation bypass in /ftp file server

detail.text: GET /ftp/package.json.bak returns 403 ("Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!"), but GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md (URL-encoded null byte %00) returns HTTP 200 with the full contents of the restricted .bak file. The filename extension check is bypassed with a null byte, allowing download of arbitrary non-.md/.pdf files from the /ftp directory (which also lists sensitive files such as coupons_2013.md.bak, incident-support.kdbx, package-lock.json.bak). Encoded path traversal (/ftp/%2e%2e%2f...) is rejected by nginx with 400.

leads.title: [agent] SQL injection in /rest/products/search q parameter (SQLite, UNION-exploitable)

detail.text: The q parameter of GET /rest/products/search is concatenated into a SQLite query. A quote triggers a 500 SQLITE_ERROR leaking the query (...LIKE '%<q>%' OR description LIKE '%<q>%'...). A UNION injection q=qwert'))UNION SELECT sqlite_version(),'2','3','4','5','6','7','8','9'-- returned a row with id="3.44.2" (SQLite version) plus the injected marker columns, proving arbitrary query execution and data exfiltration (the Products table has 9 columns; the same technique can read the Users table). Read-only non-sensitive proof used; credentials were not dumped.

leads.title: [agent] Unauthenticated /rest/memories exposes user password hashes and tokens

detail.text: GET /rest/memories with no authentication returns photo-wall "memories" that embed the full related User object, including password (hash), email, deluxeToken, totpSecret and role for users such as the admin (bkimminich, role admin) and deluxe users. This is excessive sensitive-data exposure / broken object property level authorization on an unauthenticated endpoint. Flagged for the authorization/data-exposure lane.

leads.title: [agent] Verbose Express error pages leak stack traces and internal paths; permissive wildcard CORS

detail.text: Error responses (e.g. /redirect 406, /rest/products/search 500 SQL error, /profile 500, /rest/order-history 500) return full Express stack traces disclosing server file paths (/juice-shop/build/routes/*.js, node_modules/express/...) and framework version (Express ^4.22.1). security.txt also leaks an internal URL (http://localhost:3000/.well-known/csaf/...). All responses carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (the spoofed Origin header was not reflected, so no credentialed-CORS issue, but all API data is world-readable cross-origin). Flagged for the information-disclosure/config lane.

items.na_reason: [agent] Stored-XSS confirmation requires submitting a payload via POST (feedback/review/photo-wall), but this engagement is read-only (no writes permitted). The stored-HTML sink is documented from existing Feedbacks data for the reviewer.

[agent] No LDAP/directory backend exists; authentication and lookups are SQL-based (SQLite, confirmed by SQLITE_ERROR) with MongoDB for reviews. An LDAP filter payload to the search was handled as a literal string.
[agent] XML/XXE testing requires a multipart POST to /file-upload or an XML B2B order POST; writes are not permitted this run. No read-only XML-parsing input surface exists.
[agent] No XML/XPath datastore is used; data is stored in SQLite (relational, SQL errors observed) and MongoDB. There is no XPath query surface reachable via read-only requests.

[agent] No IMAP/SMTP or mail-submission interface is exposed; the contact/feedback and complaint features persist to the database and do not relay mail with user-controlled headers. No injectable mail parameters are reachable read-only.

[agent] Incubated/persistence testing requires seeding a stored payload via write operations (feedback, review, upload) and then observing delayed execution; writes are not permitted this run, so it cannot be exercised read-only.
